notes: Sweep 2026-10-22-b at head 0397dec: five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, uncommitted false, skill_hash 48939e64..., each model_id matching its tier. Every run read SKILL.md first.

Rules changed since db91c23 (git diff db91c23 -- idiomatic-elixir/): of the case's rules only Chain fallible steps with `with` changed. It is graded against the current text, where the verdict is decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and the new sentence "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result: the `with` saves the error clause and costs the reader a search for steps that are not there." Its example is now a public def build(rows) with a one-step with. Both of sonnet-1's with blocks have exactly that shape: apply_code/2 at line 85 and total/2 at line 116 are public functions whose first step is the only fallible call and whose body builds the result. A run with no `with` is "not exercised", as in the previous sweep's grade.

`with`, violating runs out of five: one-step `with` 1 of 5 (sonnet-1, twice); `else` 0 of 5; a `case` nested in a `with` body 0 of 5. The other four write no `with` and handle each single fallible call with case (opus-1 lines 71-74, haiku-1 lines 55-58, haiku-2 lines 48-51, sonnet-2 lines 74-77). In the previous sweep 1 of 5 also broke the rule (sonnet-1 there too), and opus-1 and sonnet-2 wrote two-step `with` blocks; this time no run wrote a two-step `with`, because opus-1 and sonnet-2 reject a second code in a function head instead.

Unchanged rules graded to the previous sweep's standard: Update structs, Convert external strings to atoms, Return {:ok, value} or {:error, reason}, Store and compute money, Naming (the Naming text has not changed since db91c23), Before you finish. As before, a total function that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU counts as clean under the return-tuple rule when its @doc says so (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-2), and Map.put/3 on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the struct-update pattern the rule forbids.

Before you finish: 0 of 5 violated, with one judgment call. Sonnet-1 ran mix format && mix test after its Write calls, then mix credo --strict, but no separate mix compile. The mix test output, shown in full, compiled the app with no warnings ("==> shop / Compiling 1 file (.ex) / Generated shop app"). Step 2 says "Compile, and fix every warning ... Use `mix compile` in a Mix project." The compile and its warning check did happen, so this grade calls it clean. The previous sweep's sonnet-1 also skipped Credo, so that grade does not settle this case. A stricter reading that requires the literal mix compile command would turn Sonnet to violated. The other four ran format, compile --warnings-as-errors, credo --strict and test after their last edit.

Refused commands (only commands starting with mix, elixir or elixirc were pre-approved): haiku-1 a $(find ...) listing loop and a which/ls chain; haiku-2 a find -exec listing, and two chains with $? / ${PIPESTATUS} echoes that it then re-ran as separate mix format, deps.get, compile --force --warnings-as-errors, test and credo --strict commands; opus-1 a sed/python3 heredoc that added `doctest Shop.Cart` and carried the mix chain, re-run after an Edit; sonnet-1 an xargs/cat listing, and a python3 heredoc that rewrote both files followed by mix format && mix compile && mix test; mix credo --strict, after which it wrote the files with Write and ran mix format && mix test, then mix credo --strict; sonnet-2 a cd outside its working directory and a cat >>/python3 heredoc edit, made with Edit instead. None of the refusals was a run's only attempt at Credo, and only sonnet-1 never re-ran mix compile itself (see above).

Expected reads: all five runs added tests. Four read testing.md before their first edit to test/shop/cart_test.exs (opus-1 with cat, the others with Read). Haiku-1 did not: its reads are SKILL.md only, and the transcript mentions testing.md only inside SKILL.md's own text. No run read library-design.md this time (opus-1 and sonnet-1 did in the previous sweep).

other_violations: haiku-1's test binds {:ok, cart} and then asserts cart.discount_code == :free_shipping (lines 65-67). That is the first "Instead of" shape of Assert with patterns, which predates db91c23; the rule's new pin sentence does not decide it. Opus-1 has two test pipelines with two steps on one line (lines 37 and 42), the shape the earlier grades listed under the pipeline rule. I found no break of the new do: rule. Opus-1's wrapped `def apply_discount(...) when is_binary(code),\n do:` (lines 77-78) is a head that mix format wrapped, which the rule allows. Haiku-1's discount_cents/2 block clause (lines 94-96) would be 102 characters on one line and is set apart from its do: sibling by a blank line, as the rule says to do.

Verified in scratch copies of each project (copied, then mix deps.get): mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors, mix credo --strict (no issues) and mix test pass in all five. A probe run with mix run gave these results. 2 x APPLE at 100 gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all five (sonnet-1 returns {:ok, cents}). Opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 reject a second code, and the Haiku runs replace it. Removing 5 of 2 units empties the items. BOGUS is rejected with a tagged-tuple reason in all five. Haiku-1 trims and upcases the code; the others are case-sensitive. An unpriced SKU raises KeyError except in sonnet-1, which returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}}.
